ground_truth.title: Core Architecture Review: Durable Queue & Agentic Verifier
ground_truth.reference_transcript: David: Let's begin the architectural review for our next development cycle. Elena, can you walk us through the durability issues in our current background task processing? Elena: Currently, background tasks run directly inside the FastAPI process via BackgroundTasks. If the web worker terminates or restarts mid-job during a long transcription, the processing state is lost. I propose migrating our background pipeline to an asynchronous Redis queue with persistent checkpoints after each graph node. I will build the prototype using Redis streams and persistence checkpoints by November 2nd. David: That is high priority. Priya, what about the LLM extraction accuracy? Priya: The extraction prompt occasionally outputs hallucinations or attributes action items to participants who merely asked a question. We need a second-pass verifier agent that demands an exact verbatim quote and timestamp from the transcript before accepting any action item. I will design the verifier prompt and schema validator by November 5th. David: Excellent. Now for decisions: We formally decide to require supporting transcript quotes for all extracted action items. If an item lacks supporting evidence, it must be flagged for human review. Elena: Agreed. Priya: Agreed. David: Also, we decide to adopt AES-256 GCM encryption for storing third-party user credentials like Jira and Slack tokens. I will update the security specification document by November 6th.
